questions: What am I?
I stayed still while others moved on me.
Someone saw me with his eyes closed.
In Yaakov's dream, malachim went up and down my steps.
Who am I?
I left home alone and later had a big family.
On my journey, I slept outdoors.
I dreamed of malachim going up and down a ladder.
What are we?
We needed someone to watch us.
Our shepherd had to work in heat and cold.
Rachel brought a flock of us to drink. Baa!
What am I?
Thirsty animals were close by.
A heavy cover kept them waiting.
After Yaakov moved a stone, they could drink my water.
Who am I?
I arrived while people were talking about my family.
I was bringing animals for a drink.
Yaakov met me at the well; Leah is my older sister.
What am I?
I did not change size, but I seemed very short.
Love made me feel like only a few days.
I was Yaakov's first stretch of work for Rachel.
Who am I?
A morning brought a surprise about me.
I was the older of two sisters.
Lavan gave me to Yaakov first, instead of Rachel.
Who am I?
I welcomed a relative and became his boss.
My promises were hard to trust.
Yaakov worked for me; Rachel and Leah are my daughters.
Who am I?
My arrival ended a long wait.
My mother hoped for another son after me.
I am Rachel's first son, born in this parsha.
Who am I?
My mother spoke of thanks when I was born.
Three brothers came before me.
I am Leah's fourth son; my name recalls thanking Hashem.
What am I?
I stood up after a night of lying down.
Oil was poured on my top.
Yaakov set me up as a monument after his dream.
Who am I?
I brought my mother something from a field.
Rachel asked her to share what I found.
I found dudaim; I am Yaakov and Leah's oldest son.
What number am I?
I count years, not sons or sheep.
Fourteen of me were for marriage; six were for flocks.
I am Yaakov's total years working for Lavan.
Where am I?
My new name remembered a special night.
Yaakov called me the house of Hashem.
I was once called Luz; my new name is Beis ___.
What are we?
Our colors helped decide who would own us.
Some of us had spots or speckles.
We were animals in the flocks that became Yaakov's wages.
silly_round: Yaakov dreamed of an elevator full of penguins.
The sheep waited for someone to turn on the kitchen tap.
A stone had to be moved from the well.
Lavan gave Yaakov Rachel at the first wedding, just as promised.
Yaakov said, "I worked for you for twenty minutes!"
notes: Easy answers stay familiar. Clues progress from indirect to concrete; no answer-name giveaways.
